findings.note: Barnes made 0 threes in 2 of his last 5 games (Nov 1 and Nov 2, 0-3 each) and took only 2-3 threes in four of those five, which leaves a real chance of a 0-make night; he made 1, 4 and 1 in the other three games.
When Barnes came back from his groin injury on Nov 15, he went 4-8 from three in 36 minutes, hit a step-back three to force overtime, and RotoWire expects him to be Toronto's No. 1 option on offense.

Barnes (groin) is due back Friday after a one-game absence, while RJ Barrett (hamstring) misses his second straight game and Kawhi Leonard is still out, so Barnes may have more shots to take, threes included.

NBA.com news from Nov 19, 2026 says Poeltl went back into the starting five against Washington after two bench games. In that start he had 8 points and 5 assists in 29 minutes, for 13 points plus assists, which clears 12.5.

RotoWire notes on CBS show his two starts with 31 minutes produced 21 (Nov 7 vs MIL) and 20 (Nov 10 vs MEM) points plus assists. They also show a left shoulder bursitis issue that cost him two games in early November and a minutes split with Murray-Boyles.

ESPN lists his 2026-27 averages at 8.1 points and 1.6 assists, about 9.7 combined, which is below the 12.5 line. NBA.com's game log shows he stayed under 12.5 in four of his last five games (4, 7, 12, 12, then 13).

In his most recent game (Nov 18 vs. Hawks) Mitchell scored 13 points with 6 assists in 34 minutes, which is 19 points+assists, under 21.5; CBS says his scoring has dipped, but the Thunder's backcourt injuries should keep giving him chances.

His player page lists season averages of 18.5 points and 3.3 assists, about 21.8 combined and right at the line; he has a recent left ankle sprain that kept him out Nov 14 vs. the Clippers, and he was questionable before returning Nov 16.
On Nov 6 he scored a season-high 35 points with 5 assists. At that point he averaged 19.7 points and 3.7 assists, about 23.4 combined, in a bigger role with Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace out.

Poeltl averages 8.1 PPG this season and scored 8, 3, 11, 9 and 6 in his last five games, with 17-32 minutes. He came off the bench for two games, then returned to the starting lineup against Washington on Nov 18.

RotoWire notes there show he scored 19 on Nov 7 and 18 on Nov 10, playing 31 minutes in each, after injuries opened up minutes. He has also been dealing with left shoulder bursitis, and Collin Murray-Boyles has been taking a large share of the center minutes.
From last season (March 2026): Poeltl scored 21 points on 9-12 shooting with 18 rebounds in 36 minutes in a win over the Pistons, so he has had a big game against this opponent before.

In the Nov 18 loss to Atlanta he had 13 pts, 6 reb and 6 ast (25 PRA, just under 25.5) in about 34 minutes; CBS notes his scoring has dipped but says OKC's backcourt injuries should keep giving him opportunities.

Profile shows 2026 averages of 18.5 pts, 3.6 reb and 3.3 ast (about 25.4 PRA, right at the line); Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are expected to miss extended time, and he recently sat with a left ankle sprain before returning.
Before the ankle sprain he scored a season-high 35 vs Memphis and was averaging 19.7 pts, 3.7 reb and 3.7 ast (about 27 PRA) in 27.9 minutes, which points to a ceiling well above 25.5.
